# AI rules — Main Process (Node/TypeScript)

Governs all code under `src/main/` and `src/shared/`. Derived from real bugs, SDK
uplifts, and decisions recorded in `docs/chats/` and `docs/design/`.
See [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) §4 for component structure and §7 for
stability zones; renderer-side rules are in [AI_FRONTEND.md](AI_FRONTEND.md),
packaging in [AI_ELECTRON.md](AI_ELECTRON.md).

---

## 1. Pi SDK Integration (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` + `@earendil-works/pi-ai`)

### Version Management

- **Always version-lock both packages.** They ship from one repo and must be
  uplifted together; a mismatch produces type errors and runtime failures.
  Currently pinned to **0.87.1** in `package.json` (`dependencies`).
- The old `@mariozechner/pi-*` scope was deprecated at 0.73.1; this app migrated
  to `@earendil-works/pi-*` at 0.74.0. Do not reintroduce the old scope.
- Both are pre-1.0 — breaking changes land between minors. Budget adaptation time
  on every uplift.
- Verify against the installed package, not memory: docs ship at
  `<pkg>/docs/` (`models.md`, `sdk.md`, `settings.md`), type definitions at
  `<pkg>/dist/**/*.d.ts`, and `index.d.ts` re-exports the real surface from
  `dist/core/sdk.d.ts`. Resolve the path with `require.resolve`, never hardcode it.
- Uplift history that forced code changes (0.60→0.71): TypeBox migration
  (`@sinclair/typebox` → `typebox`), `ModelRegistry` static → instance method,
  `appendSystemPrompt` `string` → `string[]`, `tools` → `customTools` in
  `createAgentSession`, event-type renames in the subscribe callback. Later
  minors (0.80, 0.82, 0.85.1) needed no source change — verify that claim, don't
  assume it. 0.87.1 looked source-free too and was not: since 0.86 pi reports a
  `system` message with empty content (its tool declaration, from
  `declareToolChanges` in `pi-agent-core/dist/agent-loop.js`) through `message_end`,
  and `resolveMessageEndPayload` (`src/main/claude/agent-runner-message-end.ts`)
  showed it as an empty model result until it learned to skip non-assistant roles;
  a cast on the event's message hid the new role from `typecheck`, and no test
  covered a non-assistant role.

### The SDK-only boundary — in-memory session & settings managers

`createAgentSession` is called with `PiSessionManager.inMemory()` and
`PiSettingsManager.inMemory({...})` (`src/main/claude/agent-runner.ts:3404-3407`).
The rationale — why a persisting manager would couple us to the `pi` CLI's
workflow — is in [ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md) §4.1. Read it before touching
either call.

**Rules:**

- Every SDK uplift must re-assert both `inMemory()` calls. The SDK defaults are
  CLI-shaped, so a mechanical migration silently re-introduces the coupling rather
  than failing loudly.
- We own history instead: `sessions` / `messages` / `trace_steps` in
  `<userData>/data/cowork.db` (see §4).
- Regression coverage lives in `tests/sdk-only-session-isolation.test.ts`. Keep it
  green; it is the only guard on this boundary.

### Public surface vs. private reach-arounds

- Prefer the public extension points: `piSession.subscribe()`,
  `setModel()`, `setThinkingLevel()`, `prompt(text, options)`,
  `dispose()`, and the `tool_call` extension event.
- **One reach-around remains**: `installPermissionHook` reads
  `(piSession as any).agent` (`agent-runner.ts:1586`) to reach the agent's
  existing `beforeToolCall` hook. It is guarded by
  `before-tool-call-hook.ts`, which **throws** rather than logging when no known
  hook shape is found — a future SDK break must fail loudly, not silently drop the
  permission gate. Keep that fail-closed behaviour.
- Never add a second reach-around without documenting the risk and the exact SDK
  version tested against.

### Session lifecycle

- One `createAgentSession()` per chat session, cached in `this.piSessions`, keyed
  by session id, LRU-evicted at `MAX_CACHED_SESSIONS = 50`
  (`agent-runner.ts:631`). Eviction calls `session.dispose()`.
- Reused sessions hot-swap model and thinking level through public setters
  (`agent-runner.ts:3222-3247`); a swap also refreshes the Ollama `num_ctx` ref.
- `buildPiSessionRuntimeSignature()` (`src/main/claude/pi-session-runtime.ts`)
  fingerprints config provider, custom protocol, model provider/api/baseUrl,
  effective cwd, a **SHA-256 of the API key** (never the key itself), and the
  workspace-instructions file content. A mismatch forces recreation. **If your
  feature adds state that must invalidate a cached session, add it to the
  signature input.**
- On reuse, the mutable `cwdRef.value` is updated before `prompt()` so the
  permission hook resolves paths against the current cwd. The SDK runs prompts
  sequentially per session, which is what makes that safe mid-run.
- `piSession.prompt(text, options?)` is the only entry point for user messages.
  Pass `options.images` for multimodal input — never inline base64 in the text.

### Tool wiring — how tools actually reach the SDK

Verified shape (`agent-runner.ts:3194-3400`):

```
createCodingTools(effectiveCwd)                       ← SDK built-ins (read/write/edit/bash/glob/grep)
  → wrapBashToolWithDefaultTimeout(...)               ← 120s default when the model omits one
  → wrapBashToolForSudo(withTimeout, sessionId, cwd)   ← intercepts sudo, requests password
  → passed to createAgentSession as customTools

createAgentSession({ noTools: 'builtin', customTools: [...built-ins, ...mcp, ...extensions] })
```

- `noTools: 'builtin'` disables the SDK's own default tools
  (`dist/core/sdk.d.ts:30-33`: "disable the default built-in tools (read, bash,
  edit, write) but keep extension/custom tools enabled"). The app supplies its
  **wrapped** built-ins instead, so every tool passes the same wrappers. Do not
  drop `noTools` — unwrapped duplicates would bypass the wrappers.
- MCP tools are rebuilt every run so added/removed servers take effect
  immediately: `buildMcpCustomTools()` → `filterMcpCustomTools()` (workspace and
  session overrides) → `wrapMcpToolsWithTimeout()` (per-server timeout returning
  a structured error instead of hanging). `filterMcpCustomTools` must run before
  the timeout wrapper.
- Extension tools come from `AgentRuntimeExtensionManager` (`src/main/extensions/`)
  and are appended last.
- `wrapBashToolForSudo` returns 5-param `execute` while `createAgentSession`
  expects 4-param; the extra context arg is simply not passed. The cast is
  commented at the call site — keep the comment if you touch it.

**Rules for new wrappers:**

- Always call `originalExecute` on the happy path — never silently swallow.
- On deny/error return a well-formed tool-result object rather than throwing, so
  the model can recover. (Throwing _is_ correct for the missing-agent guard in
  §1, which must refuse to start the session.)
- Fail closed, never open: an unreadable or malformed permission response denies.
- Log at info level: tool name, session id, decision.

### Permission gate installation

- `installPermissionHook(piSession, sessionId, cwdRef)` runs **once per newly
  created session** (`agent-runner.ts:3417`) — the hook persists across reuses, so
  re-installing is not just wasteful, it recaptures an already-wrapped hook.
- The gate is installed through the SDK's `tool_call` extension event and
  delegates to the captured SDK hook on the allow path, preserving extension
  tool_call events and the SDK's internal queue.
- The `beforeToolCall` hook is where async user interaction (permission dialogs)
  belongs. Never do it in `subscribe()` — blocking the SDK event queue is a
  known cause of renderer state desync (see §9).
- Known limitation, documented at the call site: the async permission wait can
  make the renderer miss UI update events, so a loading spinner may not clear even
  though the tool ran. Diagnose renderer-side; do not "fix" it by making the hook
  synchronous.

### Thinking levels

- `src/shared/thinking-levels.ts` is the single source of truth: the ordered list
  `['off','minimal','low','medium','high','xhigh','max']`, mirroring
  `EXTENDED_THINKING_LEVELS` in `@earendil-works/pi-ai/dist/models.js`.
- The renderer cannot import pi-ai (main-process-only dependency), so
  `clampToSupportedLevel()` **reimplements** pi's `clampThinkingLevel` search
  order. It must stay equivalent — upward first, then downward. If the two
  disagree, Settings shows one level while the agent runs at another.
  Re-verify the algorithm against pi's source on every pi uplift; the comment
  records the version it was last checked against.
- Never hardcode a level list in a component, the config store, or the runner.

### Ready-made setups and the catalog

- `COMMON_PROVIDER_SETUPS` (`src/shared/api-provider-guidance.ts`) is a hand-kept
  list of ready-made setups for a custom endpoint. It is **older than the provider
  catalog**, and the catalog is built from the installed pi (`getProviders()` /
  `getModels()`), so it grows with every pi version. A service that has a setup
  can become a catalog provider; a custom endpoint made from that setup is then
  the same provider under another name, holding a second copy of its key.
- A setup whose address is a catalog provider's own — same service, same
  protocol — names that provider in `catalogProvider` (read it through
  `catalogProviderOfSetup`). The Providers tab sends such an address to the
  provider's own entry and leaves the setup out of the list it offers. A setup
  that is only the same company on another route — another path, another
  protocol — stays a custom endpoint.
- **Re-check the list against the catalog on every pi uplift, and change it where
  the catalog has caught up.** The check is a test, not something to remember:
  `tests/provider-setups-vs-catalog.test.ts` reads the **installed** pi's
  provider data — the one test that depends on it on purpose — and fails when the
  catalog providers found on a setup's host are no longer the ones recorded
  there. A failure after an uplift means "decide again", not "broken": look at
  what changed, set or clear `catalogProvider`, and bring the test's two tables
  up to date. The reasons for the current decisions are written beside them
  (last checked against pi 0.87.1).
- The test only sees a provider that serves from a setup's **host**. A service
  that pi starts to list under a different address is not caught by it; when a
  new provider turns up in the catalog, look through the list for its name too.

### Compaction budget

- `src/main/claude/compaction-budget.ts` computes `reserveTokens` covering output
  **plus tool-schema payloads** plus a margin, because pi's built-in
  `shouldCompact` only compares conversation tokens against
  `contextWindow - reserveTokens` and does not count tool definitions.
- Tool schema tokens are estimated as `JSON.stringify(schema).length / 4`.
- Do not revert to pi's default reserve — MCP tool schemas routinely reach 20K+
  tokens and requests then 400 before compaction ever fires.

## 2. IPC Patterns (`src/main/index.ts`)

- Two generic entry points plus many typed channels:
  - `ipcMain.on('client-event', ...)` — fire-and-forget from the renderer
  - `ipcMain.handle('client-invoke', ...)` — request/response
  - ~150 direct `ipcMain.handle(channel, ...)` registrations for typed operations
    (`config.*`, `mcp.*`, `sandbox.*`, `skills.*`, `memory.*`, `schedule.*`, …).
    Count drifts upward constantly — grep before claiming a number.
- Namespace new channels with a dot-separated subsystem prefix. `src/shared/ipc-types.ts`
  holds the shared event types; the renderer union lives in
  `src/renderer/types/index.ts`.
- Main → renderer uses the `sendToRenderer` helper
  (`mainWindow.webContents.send('server-event', event)`). **Events are not
  buffered or replayed** — if the window isn't ready the event is lost. The
  renderer must hydrate from persistent state on mount rather than rely on
  catching every event.
- Renderer → main event types are allowlisted in `ALLOWED_CLIENT_EVENTS` in
  `src/preload/index.ts`; a type missing from that list is silently dropped.
- Wrap every handler body in try/catch, return structured `{ error }` objects,
  and log with `logError(message, error)`. **Never throw across the IPC
  boundary.**

## 3. MCP Tool Bridging (`src/main/mcp/`)

- `MCPManager` owns all connections (stdio / SSE / Streamable HTTP);
  `buildMcpCustomTools()` bridges them into pi's `ToolDefinition` format.
- JSON Schema from MCP tools is wrapped as TypeBox `TSchema` using the **`typebox`**
  package (renamed from `@sinclair/typebox` during the 0.60→0.71 uplift).
- **MCP servers always run on the host** — never route spawns through the
  sandbox bridges. The sandbox is for user-workspace commands only.
- `mcp-tool-permissions.ts` resolves per-tool decisions (annotations, workspace
  and session policy, recorded approvals) and is consulted by the permission
  store; a tool with no server config falls through to the generic rules and logs
  a warning — do not turn that fall-through into an allow.
- Per-server timeouts are applied by `wrapMcpToolsWithTimeout()`, which pauses and
  resumes the activity timeout around tool execution.
- Tool definitions count against the context budget; log warnings when the schema
  total gets large enough to make the budget unworkable.

## 4. SQLite Persistence

Two databases, both `better-sqlite3`, both synchronous:

| Store                | File                        | Owner                                              |
| -------------------- | --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| App (`cowork.db`)    | `<userData>/data/cowork.db` | sessions, messages, trace steps                    |
| Memory (`memory.db`) | `<storageRoot>/memory.db`   | experience memory (`MEMORY_DB_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1`) |

**Rules:**

- **Native module** — compiled against Electron's ABI. Run `npm run rebuild`
  after any Electron bump or plain `npm install` touching native deps.
- All queries are synchronous by design. Don't wrap them in `async` unless the
  function genuinely combines them with other async work.
- No migration framework: `initDatabase()` uses `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` and
  `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` guarded by try/catch for duplicate-column errors.
- Multi-statement writes use `db.transaction(...)()`.
- Close both databases on `before-quit`.
- `memory-db.ts` validates SQL identifiers against `/^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$/`
  before interpolating them into DDL. Keep that guard — table names are dynamic.
- Memory runs in WAL mode and stays separate from `cowork.db` so it can live under
  the relocatable `storageRoot`.

## 5. Memory System (`src/main/memory/`)

Stability zone: ⚠️ Experimental. As-built detail lives in
`docs/internals/memory-internals.md` and
`docs/internals/memory-system-architecture.md`; the migration rationale is
`docs/design/archive/memory-storage-sqlite-migration.md`.

- Three stores, don't conflate them: **core** memory (JSON), **experience** memory
  (SQLite + embeddings), and per-session **state** (JSON).
- `memory-service.ts` owns orchestration (ingestion queue, retriever, navigator,
  LLM client). Store modules own SQL; extractors own prompting.
- **Embedding configuration has its own gate.** `memoryRuntime.embedding` carries
  `inheritFromActive`; when a custom embedding config leaves `provider`
  undefined, code must **not** silently substitute the active _chat_ provider —
  that coupling produced real misconfiguration (design:
  `docs/design/archive/embedding-provider-gate-and-coverage.md`). Branch on the
  embedding provider id deliberately.
- `EMBEDDING_FORMAT_VERSION` (`src/shared/local-embedding-types.ts:25`) is stamped
  in the experience store. Format-staleness prompts (`isEmbeddingFormatStale()`)
  are **local-provider-gated**; remote installs never see them. Do not present
  rebuild prompts to remote-embedding users.
- **Embedding prefixes are model-specific.** `EmbeddingKind = 'query' | 'document'`
  is threaded through `embedText → embed → embedLocal`; the EmbeddingGemma prefixes
  (`task: search result | query: `, `title: none | text: `) apply **local only**.
  Remote models (OpenAI, BGE) are prefix-free. Add a new model's prefixes via a
  per-provider kind→prefix map, never inline in the service.
- Local embeddings are **sequential** by design; `ingestionConcurrency` gates only
  the LLM extraction pool. Offload to a worker thread if jank appears rather than
  lowering concurrency.
- `local-embedding-state.ts` and `local-embedding-cache.ts` must stay free of
  `@huggingface/transformers` imports so IPC and startup don't load the ML
  runtime. Keep the ML runtime behind lazy import in
  `local-embedding-provider.ts` (singleton pipeline, cache under
  `{storageRoot}/models`, dtype fallback q8 → fp16 → fp32, pinned model revision,
  dimension validated after each inference).
- Per-row `embedding_model` is stamped on store rows; retrieval filters on
  it so a model change can't silently compare vectors from two models.

## 6. Config Store (`src/main/config/config-store.ts`)

- `electron-store` with encrypted-at-rest storage and key rotation
  (`src/main/utils/store-encryption.ts`).
- `configStore.get(key)` / `getAll()` / `update(partial)`.
- Adding a config field requires all of:
  1. the `AppConfig` type,
  2. `defaultConfig` with a safe default,
  3. the `normalizeConfig` path with validation/coercion,
  4. `DIRECT_READ_KEYS` if readable without `getAll()`,
  5. the `update()` persistence block (top-level scalars and the `memoryRuntime`
     llm/embedding sub-objects merge field-by-field — read the comment before
     adding to either),
  6. the mirrored type in `src/renderer/types/index.ts`.
- Fresh-install vs. upgraded-install defaults differ deliberately (schema-v2 memory
  defaults). Keep the branch explicit when touching defaults; silently applying
  new defaults to existing installs changes behaviour mid-upgrade.
- Config that affects a live agent session must be reflected in the pi runtime
  signature (§1) or a cached session keeps stale state.
- The renderer owns settings UI state. Main-process caches
  (`permission-rules-store.ts`) are hydrated from the renderer via the
  `settings.update` event at bootstrap; defaults apply before first hydration.

## 7. Permission System

- `permission-rules-store.ts` caches `PermissionRule[]` from the renderer and is
  the main-process decision point. **Renderer-originated settings are untrusted at
  this boundary** — `sanitizeRules()` validates and coerces everything, with
  unknown actions falling back to `'ask'` so the worst case is an extra prompt.
- `decidePermission(sessionId, toolName, input)` → `'allow' | 'deny' | 'ask'`.
  Matching order: bash lists (authoritative when non-empty) → trusted directories
  (bash visible writes; `write` / `edit` paths) → session-scoped "always allow"
  memory → first matching rule → default `'ask'`.
  `decidePermissionDetailed()` returns the same action plus the reason for an
  `ask`; the permission hook passes that reason to the dialog.
- **Trusted directories** (`trustedDirectories`, the write zone) sit before the
  session memory on purpose: one "Allow always" click must not cover writes
  outside the list. For bash they only add an `ask` — they never turn the lists'
  `ask` into `allow`. For `write` / `edit`, inside → `allow` (a user `deny` rule
  still wins), outside → `ask`. The app's own settings file always asks
  (`setProtectedWriteFiles`). Design: `docs/design/trusted-directories.md`.
- MCP tools resolve through `mcp-tool-permissions.ts` (annotations, workspace and
  session policy, recorded approvals).
- Session-scoped "always allow" is dropped via `forgetSessionPermissions()` on
  session delete.
- **The bash engine is one source of truth**, shared by the app and the `pi` CLI
  extension: `src/shared/bash-restrictions/` (`scan.ts`, `engine.ts`,
  `write-zone.ts`, `settings.ts`).
  Edit it once, never fork a copy into a host. `permission-rules-store.ts` imports
  from it — do not reimplement matching logic locally. Its `index.ts` stays free of
  file-system imports; `write-zone.ts` (which resolves real paths) is imported by its
  own path, never re-exported from the barrel. Semantics are documented in
  `BASH_COMMAND_RESTRICTIONS.md`. The extension must never enter the Electron main
  bundle.
- **Command text is read in exactly one place:** `scanBashCommand` in `scan.ts`.
  The syntax guard, the splitter and the write-target check all consume its
  result. Do not add a second parser, a regex over the raw command, or a
  "quick check" beside it — two readers that disagree about what a command says
  is the whole class of bypass. The property to keep: text the shell executes is
  never classified as inert (single-quoted strings, quoted-delimiter here-document
  bodies and dropped comment lines are the only inert regions). When unsure, the
  scanner reports the command as unsupported and the engine asks.
  `tests/bash-restrictions-multiline.test.ts` holds the adversarial cases.

## 8. Security Boundaries

**Path containment**

- `isPathWithinRoot()` (defined in `src/shared/path-permissions/containment.ts`,
  re-exported from `src/main/tools/path-containment.ts`) rejects `..`
  traversal, symlink escape, and absolute paths outside the workspace. Used by the
  executors, `PathGuard`, the workspace-instructions loader, and the trusted-directories
  write zone.
- Resolve with `fs.realpathSync` before comparing, or symlink escape passes. For a
  path that may not exist yet (a write target), use `realpathExistingPortion()` from
  `src/shared/path-permissions/` — it also follows a link whose destination does not
  exist yet, which a plain "resolve the parent" does not.
- `resolveToolPath()` in the same module **mirrors** pi's unexported `resolveToCwd`
  (how `write` / `edit` resolve their `path`). If the mirror drifts, the check
  approves one path while the tool writes another.
  `tests/path-permissions-pi-parity.test.ts` compares the two against the installed
  package — on a pi upgrade, fix the mirror, never the test.

**Sandbox adapter**

- `SandboxAdapter` routes execution to WSL2 / Lima / Native by platform and config;
  `sandboxEnabled` is `false` by default, so everything runs natively today.
- `PathGuard` blocks escape from the session sandbox directory inside VMs.
- Never route MCP server spawns through the sandbox.
- `getUnsupportedWorkspacePathReason()` rejects UNC paths on Windows when the
  sandbox is enabled. Validate workspace paths before accepting them as
  `effectiveCwd`.

**Rules:** these three areas — path containment, permission gating, and the
renderer/main IPC boundary — exist to stop an LLM-driven agent from executing
unapproved actions. Don't loosen, bypass, or stub them to make a check pass.

---

## 9. Event Subscribe Pattern (`src/main/claude/agent-runner.ts`)

`piSession.subscribe(callback)` is the central event router — streaming deltas,
tool traces, turn/agent boundaries, compaction events.

- **Never block inside the callback.** It runs synchronously in the SDK's event
  queue; awaiting a dialog there disrupts ordering and desyncs renderer state.
  Async user interaction belongs in the tool `execute` wrapper or the
  `beforeToolCall` gate (§1).
- The handler calls `sendMessage()`, which persists to the DB and forwards to the
  renderer. A successful DB write does **not** guarantee the renderer received the
  event — IPC is fire-and-forget and unbuffered.
- The guard modules (`mid-loop-overflow-guard.ts`, `pre-request-guard.ts`,
  `read-loop-guard.ts`, `tool-error-enrichment.ts`) exist because real models
  misbehave: they loop on reads, overflow mid-loop, and emit opaque tool errors.
  When you touch the tool path, keep these in the chain and keep them failing
  closed.

---

## 10. Cold-Start History Rebuild

When a session is reopened and the in-memory SDK session has no history, the
runner rebuilds a `<conversation_history>` preamble from DB messages.

- Budget: `0.3 × contextWindow` (`0.15` for small Ollama models).
- Token estimation: `text.length / 4` — systematically underestimates CJK and
  dense JSON. Known limitation, documented in place.
- Serialize `text`, `thinking` (as `<thinking>` tags), `tool_use`, and
  `tool_result`. **Do not filter to `type === 'text'`** — that filter caused a
  real DeepSeek 400 on cold start, because thinking models require
  `reasoning_content` on every assistant message.
- Images are excluded — too large for the preamble budget.

---

## 11. Other Main-Process Subsystems

- **Schedule** (`src/main/schedule/`, types shared via `src/shared/schedule/`) —
  cron-like tasks with daily/weekly/interval repeat, a tick loop, time windows,
  catch-up, budgets, and run history, persisted as `ScheduledTask` rows.
  Execution delegates to the session manager. Time-window maths is pure and lives
  in `time-window.ts` — keep it pure so it stays testable.
- **Runtime extensions** (`src/main/extensions/`) — pluggable per-session hooks
  (`beforeSessionRun`, `afterSessionRun`, `sessionDeleted`) contributing custom
  tools. The manager merges tools by name in a `Map`, so **later registrations
  win**; register in a deterministic order or you'll chase phantom
  last-writer-wins bugs.
- **Session titles** (`src/main/session/`) — generation flow split from pure
  helpers (`session-title-utils.ts` + `src/shared/session-title.ts`) so
  normalization and the prompt builder are testable without a session.
- **Chat export** (`src/main/chat/`) — one native save dialog with every format
  filter, then dispatch on file extension (`export-router.ts`). Adding a format
  means a new filter entry **and** a new dispatch case — the format is a parameter
  of the export, not a separate action.
- **Workspace orphan detection** (`src/main/workspace/`) — finds stale skill/MCP
  references in `.cowork/*.json` after a skill or server is removed. Runs once per
  workspace activation (cwd change or session start), piggybacking on
  already-loaded data — do not move it into a per-message path.
- **Migration** (`src/main/migration/`) — bootstrap and legacy-data migration at
  startup. Anything that reads old on-disk layout lives here, not in a subsystem.

---

## 12. `src/shared/` — code that crosses a boundary

Shared between main, renderer, and (for some of it) the `pi` CLI extension. The
organizing rule is **which host can load it**:

| Module                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Constraint                                                                                              |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `provider-catalog.ts`, `provider-ids.ts`, `thinking-levels.ts`, `ipc-types.ts`, `mcp-tool-classification.ts`, `local-embedding-types.ts`, `workspace-*.ts`, `session-title.ts`, `skill-*.ts`, `network/` | Renderer-safe: **no pi-ai / electron imports**, pure types and helpers.                                 |
| `bash-restrictions/`                                                                                                                                                                                     | Also consumed by the `pi` extension — must stay Node-standalone, no electron, no app config.            |
| `path-permissions/`                                                                                                                                                                                      | Same as `bash-restrictions/`, and **not renderer-safe**: it uses `node:fs`. Main + `pi` extension only. |
| `permission-reason.ts`                                                                                                                                                                                   | Renderer-safe by construction: type-only imports. Keep them `import type`.                              |
| `api-model-presets.ts`, `api-provider-guidance.ts`, `ollama-base-url.ts`                                                                                                                                 | Main + renderer, but no electron runtime access.                                                        |

- **Never import pi-ai or electron from `src/shared/`.** That is exactly why
  `thinking-levels.ts` reimplements pi's clamp instead of calling it, and why the
  provider catalog splits into a shared half and
  `src/main/config/provider-catalog-native.ts` (built from
  `getProviders()` / `getModels()`, delivered over IPC as
  `config.getProviderCatalog`).
- Native provider catalog entries are built in main and shipped over IPC; the
  renderer never queries pi-ai directly. Keep it that way.
- The `pi` extension (`pi-extensions/`) must never enter the Electron main bundle.

---

## 13. Dependency Upgrade Checklist

Before upgrading any Tier 1 dependency (see `docs/dependency-tiers.md`):

1. Read the release notes for breaking changes.
2. Check whether `pi-ai` and `pi-coding-agent` need a coordinated uplift.
3. Run `npm run typecheck` — catch type-level breaks.
4. Run `npm test` — catch behavioural breaks.
5. Manually test: new session, tool use, session reuse, compaction trigger,
   permission prompt, stop/cancel.
6. For `better-sqlite3`: `npm run rebuild` after any Electron bump.
7. Update `docs/dependency-tiers.json` with the new installed version.
8. Re-assert the `inMemory()` session/settings boundary (§1).
9. Re-verify `clampToSupportedLevel` against the new pi-ai source (§1).
10. Re-check the ready-made provider setups against the catalog the new pi brings
    (§1, "Ready-made setups and the catalog"). A failing
    `tests/provider-setups-vs-catalog.test.ts` is the prompt to do it, not a
    regression to patch around.
11. Document adaptations in the commit message body.

**`allowScripts` is a hard gate in this repo.** `package.json` allowlists
install scripts by **exact version** (`"electron@41.10.7": true`, …). Bump
`electron`, `sharp`, `better-sqlite3`, `onnxruntime-node`, `esbuild`, `protobufjs`
or `electron-winstaller` **in the same edit**. Miss it and npm reports one warning
line among many, the postinstall never runs, and the native payload is simply
absent — for `electron` that means an empty `node_modules/electron/dist/` and an
app that won't start. Fixing the entry alone isn't enough: a plain `npm install`
doesn't re-run a script for an already-unpacked package, so follow up with
`npm rebuild <pkg>`.

- `sharp` additionally needs an `overrides` entry to move at all — upstream pins an
  older range.
- **Never run `npm audit fix --force` here.** It doesn't know about `allowScripts`,
  and every remedy it proposes today is a downgrade that either fixes nothing or
  costs a feature. CI runs `npm audit --audit-level=critical --omit=dev || true`
  for exactly this reason; the remaining findings are documented rather than
  force-fixed.

---

## 14. Common Pitfalls (from real bugs)

| Bug / trap                                               | Root cause                                                     | Rule                                                                          |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Sessions leak into the `pi` CLI's session list           | An uplift reverted to the SDK's persisting `SessionManager`    | Re-assert `PiSessionManager.inMemory()` + `PiSettingsManager.inMemory()` (§1) |
| Settings shows level X, agent runs at Y                  | `clampToSupportedLevel` drifted from pi's `clampThinkingLevel` | Keep the mirror exact; re-verify on uplift (§1)                               |
| A custom endpoint duplicates a catalog provider          | A ready-made setup's service became a catalog provider in pi   | Re-check `COMMON_PROVIDER_SETUPS` on every pi uplift; the test fails (§1)     |
| Images not visible to the LLM                            | `prompt(text)` only — image blocks never passed                | Pass `options.images`                                                         |
| DeepSeek 400 on cold start                               | History rebuild filtered out `thinking` blocks                 | Serialize every content-block type (§10)                                      |
| Permission dialog breaks renderer state                  | Async wait inside the SDK's `beforeToolCall` / subscribe queue | Async interaction in the execute wrapper only (§1, §9)                        |
| Context overflow 400                                     | Compaction threshold ignored tool-schema tokens                | Use `compaction-budget.ts`, never pi's default reserve (§1)                   |
| Session runs a stale system prompt                       | Cached pi session kept the old `appendSystemPrompt`            | Put the new state in the runtime signature (§1)                               |
| Request past the context limit, MCP schemas huge         | Tool schemas not counted in compaction                         | See compaction budget above                                                   |
| A tool wrapper silently no-ops                           | `originalExecute` not called on the happy path                 | Always delegate; fail closed on deny (§1)                                     |
| `better-sqlite3` fails to load after `npm install`       | Native module built against host Node ABI                      | `npm run rebuild` (§4, §13)                                                   |
| App won't start after an `electron` bump                 | `allowScripts` version drift — postinstall blocked             | Update `allowScripts` in the same edit, then `npm rebuild electron` (§13)     |
| MCP tools fail inside the sandbox                        | Spawn routed through the Lima/WSL bridge                       | MCP always runs on host (§3)                                                  |
| Retrieval silently returns nothing after a model change  | Vectors from two models compared as one                        | Per-row `embedding_model` filter (§5)                                         |
| Remote-embedding user gets a "rebuild embeddings" prompt | Format-staleness check not gated on local provider             | Gate on provider id (§5)                                                      |
